The Jerónimos Monastery in Belém, Lisbon, was begun in 1501 by King Manuel I near the spot from which Vasco da Gama had sailed for India.

It was paid for largely by a tax on the spice trade with Asia. It is the finest work of the Manueline style, a late Gothic style full of carved ropes, sea creatures, armillary spheres and exotic plants, which celebrated the voyages. The monks prayed for sailors.

Vasco da Gama and Camões are buried there. The monastery and the nearby Tower of Belém survived the earthquake of 1755 and are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Lisbon Treaty of the European Union was signed there in 2007. See Portugal.
sum: The Jerónimos Monastery in Belém, Lisbon, was begun in 1501 by King Manuel I near the spot from which Vasco da Gama had sailed for India.
